text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Richard Holbrooke, Vice President of Credit Suisse First Boston, said the current tension between Switzerland and the U.S. due to the Nazi gold situation is the worst in the history of the countries' bilateral relations. - Swiss automobile sales dropped by 9.4 percent to 28,283 in May compared to May 1996. - The European Commission is reviewing the acquisition of Minit International SA (Mister Minit) by UBS Capital BV. TAGES ANZEIGER - Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger said he intends to toughen the government's savings programmes and cut the 8.7 billion Swiss franc deficit to six billion by next year, then to one billion by the year 2001. - Swiss financier Werner K. Rey has for the seventh time filed for release from prison. Rey has been imprisoned on the Bahamas for 14 months. - Migros Bank is cutting mortgage rates by one fourth to four percent, the lowest rate since 1980. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Shares of Sulzer Medica will be traded on the stock exchange starting mid-July. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
